name: Two Towers
description: You have two towers made of blocks, standing next to each other. Initially, the height of the first tower is $$$a$$$, and the height of the second tower is $$$b$$$. In one action, you can: take one block and place it on one of the towers, increasing its height by $$$1$$$; or take two blocks and place one on each tower, increasing both heights by $$$1$$$. However, this can only be done if their heights are equal. Your goal is to make the height of the first tower equal to $$$c$$$, and the height of the second tower equal to $$$d$$$. What is the minimum number of actions you need to perform?
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. Each test case consists of one line containing $$$4$$$ integers $$$a, b, c, d$$$ ($$$1 \le a \le c \le 10^8$$$; $$$1 \le b \le d \le 10^8$$$).
output_specification: For each test case, output one integer — the minimum number of actions that you have to perform.
approach_summary: Identify exchange argument or greedy choice property. Sort elements by payoff ratio or deadline and greedily pick candidates to achieve global optimum.
